scenarios.editor.outlineOnlyNote: This scenario has no Start node, so the step editor cannot draw it. Its steps are listed in order, following their edges; you can edit each step's settings, not how they connect.
scenarios.editor.issue.missingStart: This scenario has no Start node, so it cannot run.
scenarios.editor.issue.multipleStart: There is more than one Start node: only the first starts the run. Another Start runs as an ordinary step, and only if an edge leads into it.
scenarios.editor.issue.edgeIntoStart: An edge leads back into Start. It is followed, but the run goes on along Start's first branch only; the parallel branches start only when the run begins.
scenarios.editor.issue.edgeOutOfEnd: An edge leaves an End node; it is never followed.
scenarios.editor.issue.extraOutgoing: Step {{n}} ({{title}}) has several next steps, but only Start runs branches in parallel: at run time only the first one runs.
scenarios.editor.issue.unpickableHandle: Step {{n}} ({{title}}) has an edge it never takes: its handle is none of the cases or options the step can pick, so the edge is never followed.
scenarios.editor.issue.duplicateHandle: Step {{n}} ({{title}}) has several edges with the handle {{handle}}: only the first one runs, so the others are never followed.
scenarios.editor.issue.danglingEdge: An edge points at a step that does not exist; that branch ends there.
scenarios.editor.issue.unreachable: Step {{n}} ({{title}}) is not reached from Start, so it never runs.

scenarios.editor.issue.noCallHeld: Step {{n}} ({{title}}) needs a CSMS call its branch took over (a CSMS Call Trigger with behavior “replace” earlier in the same branch), but on some path there is none: the run fails there.
scenarios.editor.issue.noResponseHeld: Step {{n}} ({{title}}) reads the answer to an OCPP call (response…), but on some path no OCPP Call step comes before it in the same branch: the run fails there.
scenarios.editor.issue.unknownMatcher: Step {{n}} ({{title}}) has a $match in {{handle}} with an operator the simulator does not know: the run fails when the switch runs.
scenarios.editor.issue.badMatcherArgumen: Step {{n}} ({{title}}) has a $match in {{handle}} with an argument of the wrong type (or no operator): the run fails when the switch runs.
scenarios.editor.issue.unreachableCase: Step {{n}} ({{title}}): {{handle}} can never be picked, an earlier case is identical or matches every value.
scenarios.editor.issue.callAlreadyAnswer: Step {{n}} ({{title}}) answers a CSMS call that its branch has already answered on some path: the run fails there.
scenarios.editor.issue.callLeftOpen: Step {{n}} ({{title}}) takes over a CSMS call that its branch can leave unanswered; the station answers it InternalError only when the run ends. Add a Call Response (kind “none” to stay silent on purpose).

scenarios.stepHelp.statusChange: Sets the connector's status (Available, Charging, Faulted …) and reports it to the CSMS. Use it to put the connector in a known state or to simulate a change.
scenarios.stepHelp.statusNotification: Sends a StatusNotification with an explicit error code, info and vendor error code, e.g. Faulted with GroundFailure. Unlike Status Change, it does not touch the connector's own status.
scenarios.stepHelp.transaction: Starts or stops a charging transaction on the scenario's connector. A start uses the tag from a preceding Remote Start Trigger, else the one you enter; a stop can carry a stop reason.
scenarios.stepHelp.unlockOutcome: Presets how the connector answers the next UnlockConnector request: Unlocked, UnlockFailed or NotSupported. Nothing is sent now.
scenarios.stepHelp.meterValue: Sends a meter reading, or keeps sending a rising one at an interval, with optional power, charge limit and charging curve. Use it to drive energy and SoC during a session.
scenarios.stepHelp.connectorPlug: Plugs the EV cable in or out, as a driver would. Plugging in an idle connector reports Preparing; unplugging during a transaction is an EV-side disconnect.
scenarios.stepHelp.delay: Waits a fixed number of seconds, or until a given time, before the next step. Optional seeded jitter varies the wait from run to run.
scenarios.stepHelp.remoteStartTrigger: Waits for the CSMS to send a remote start request and remembers its ID tag for the next Transaction start. An optional timeout fails the run if nothing arrives.
scenarios.stepHelp.remoteStopTrigger: Waits for the CSMS to send a remote stop request, then goes on. The next Transaction stop uses its reason. An optional timeout fails the run.
scenarios.stepHelp.statusTrigger: Waits until the connector reaches a given status, e.g. Charging. It goes on at once if the connector is already there; an optional timeout ends the wait.
scenarios.stepHelp.csmsCallTrigger: Waits until the CSMS sends a chosen call (Reset, GetConfiguration …), optionally only one whose payload matches. The station still answers as usual unless a Call Response replaces the answer.
scenarios.stepHelp.reservationTrigger: Waits for the CSMS to send a reservation request, then goes on. An optional timeout fails the run if none arrives.
scenarios.stepHelp.connectionTrigger: Waits until the WebSocket connection is up or down. It does not fail when the connection drops, so it can wait out a disconnect; it only observes and never disconnects the station.
scenarios.stepHelp.switch: Compares a value (a constant, or a station field read with $from) with a list of cases and continues along the first match, else the default branch. Use it to react to the station's state or a CSMS payload.
scenarios.stepHelp.choice: Picks one of several branches at random, by weight. The draw is seeded, so the same seed takes the same path. Use it to vary runs, e.g. a mix of normal and faulty sessions.
scenarios.stepHelp.setState: Stores a value under a name that later steps read with $from state.<name>. The state belongs to the run, is shared by its parallel branches and is not kept across a restart.
scenarios.stepHelp.ocppCall: Expert: sends any OCPP call of the station's version with a payload you write, then waits for the answer. A CALLERROR is logged and the run goes on; a call the station refuses fails the run.
scenarios.stepHelp.callResponse: Answers the CSMS call this branch is holding (after a CSMS Call Trigger that replaces the answer) with a result, an error, no reply, or a plain Accepted / Rejected.
scenarios.stepHelp.notification: Sends a Heartbeat or StatusNotification with the payload you give. For any other message use OCPP Call.
scenarios.stepHelp.notify: Sends a firmware, signed firmware, log or diagnostics status notification with a status from that notification's list, then goes on without waiting for the CSMS.
scenarios.stepHelp.dataTransfer: Sends a vendor-specific DataTransfer to the CSMS with your vendor ID, an optional message ID and data.
scenarios.stepHelp.reserveNow: Creates a reservation for an ID tag on the scenario's connector, valid for a number of minutes, and sets it to Reserved. The station does it itself, as if the CSMS had asked.
scenarios.stepHelp.cancelReservation: Cancels a reservation by its ID and frees the connector if it was Reserved.
scenarios.stepHelp.configSet: Sets a configuration key to a value on the station, as if the CSMS had changed it, e.g. a shorter MeterValueSampleInterval for this scenario. Nothing is sent.
scenarios.stepHelp.useBehavior: Tunes or switches off a built-in or loaded station behavior (firmware update, logs, reset …) for this run, with optional parameters, instead of reimplementing it.
scenarios.stepHelp.responseOverride: Arms a one-shot answer for the next incoming CSMS call of a chosen action, e.g. reject the next remote start. It is used up by that call.
scenarios.stepHelp.inboundPolicy: Sets a lasting rule for an incoming CSMS call: answer with a CALLERROR, or ignore it. It survives reconnects until an Answer rule or the end of the run clears it.
scenarios.stepHelp.certQuirks: Sets or clears certificate quirks, e.g. the OCTT preset (RSA CSR, CRLF PEM, one signature algorithm), to check a CSMS against strict certification tools.
scenarios.addStep.structure.loopHelp: Repeats the steps inside it. In Steps view, drop steps into it; in Graph view, pick the step to go back to.
scenarios.editor.cannot.moveUnstable: The steps would not read back as dropped; nothing was changed.
scenarios.addStep.structure.switchHelp: Adds a branch block with a lane per case and a default lane. Drop steps into the lanes; the lanes meet again at the step that follows.
scenarios.addStep.structure.choiceHelp: Adds a branch block with two weighted options, one picked at random. Drop steps into the lanes; the lanes meet again at the step that follows.

scenarios.editor.issue.timeoutEdgeOnNonW: Step {{n}} ({{title}}) has a timeout edge, but it is not a wait with a timeout (or it ends its branch): the edge is never followed.
scenarios.editor.issue.timeoutEdgeNeverF: Step {{n}} ({{title}}) has a timeout edge, but its timeout is 0 or not set: the wait never times out, so the edge never runs.
scenarios.editor.issue.extraTimeoutEdge: Step {{n}} ({{title}}) has several timeout edges: only the first one runs when the wait times out.
scenarios.editor.issue.newerConstruct: This scenario uses a feature newer than the schema version it declares; it runs here, but an older simulator would ignore that feature.
